governing_table.code: Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code (34 Pa. Code 403.21): International Building Code of 2021, Chapter 29, Table 2902.1, the same table as Table 403.1 of the International Plumbing Code of 2021
governing_table.edition: 2021 IBC and 2021 IPC, adopted by the amendment of 34 Pa. Code 403.21 published November 2025 (55 Pa.B. 7701), effective January 1, 2026. No state amendment to Chapter 29 of the building code or Chapter 4 of the plumbing code.
governing_table.table: Table 2902.1 (building code) = Table 403.1 (plumbing code), Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures
governing_table.quote: (a) The Department adopts and incorporates by reference the following codes as the Uniform Construction Code: (1) The provisions of Chapters 2—10, 12—29 and 31—35 of the ‘‘International Building Code of 2021,’’ except: ... (6) The ‘‘International Plumbing Code of 2021’’ except: (i) A municipality within a county of the second class may not administer and enforce the ‘‘International Plumbing Code’’ adopted under this chapter. (ii) A municipality within a county of the second class that has adopted a plumbing code and accompanying rules and regulations under the Local Health Administration Law (16 P.S. § § 12001—12030) shall retain the authority to promulgate and enforce this plumbing code and to make any changes it deems necessary if the changes meet the Uniform Construction Code’s minimum requirements.
governing_table.note: The official regulation (read in full on pacodeandbulletin.gov) lists every state exception; none touches Chapter 29 of the building code or Chapter 4 of the plumbing code, so the rows are the 2021 model code's. The table rows and section texts themselves were read on a secondary copy, UpCodes 'Pennsylvania Building Code 2021' and 'Pennsylvania Plumbing Code 2021'. The regulation's exception for 'a county of the second class' is not explained on the page read; it is understood to mean Allegheny County (Pittsburgh), which keeps its own county plumbing code. That county code was NOT read: the Pittsburgh city agent must check it. The building code's Table 2902.1 (Chapter 29) is adopted statewide with no such exception.

cities_may_amend_note.text: The code applies statewide. A municipality may enact standards that equal or exceed it, after review and approval by the Department of Labor & Industry, and may keep older ordinances (in effect July 1, 1999) that equal or exceed it. So a city cannot lower these counts but may have stricter ones. Municipalities in a county of the second class keep their own plumbing code, which must meet the state minimum. Philadelphia's and Pittsburgh's own amendments were not researched here.
cities_may_amend_note.quote: (d) A municipality may retain ordinances in effect on July 1, 1999, that contain standards that equal or exceed the Uniform Construction Code under section 303(b) of the act (35 P.S. § 7210.303(b)). ... (i) A municipality may enact an ordinance containing standards that equal or exceed the Uniform Construction Code as adopted by § 403.21 (relating to the Uniform Construction Code) under section 503 of the act (35 P.S. § 7210.503) after Department review and approval.

office.wc_female: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50

restaurant.quote: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts d | 1 per 75 | 1 per 75 | [lavatories] 1 per 200 | — | 1 per 500 | 1 service sink. Footnote d: The occupant load for seasonal outdoor seating and entertainment areas shall be included when determining the minimum number of facilities required.

school.quote: 3 | Educational | Educational facilities | 1 per 50 | [lavatories] 1 per 50 | — | 1 per 100 | 1 service sink
school.note: Separate state rule for some schools: see rules.restroom_equity.

sex_split.text: Total occupant load is divided in half, unless approved statistical data shows another split. Rooms designed for all genders are counted on the total occupant load.
sex_split.quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. To determine the required number of fixtures, the fixture ratio or ratios for each fixture type shall be applied to the occupant load of each sex in accordance with Table 2902.1. ... Exceptions: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicates a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex. Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load. In such multiple-user user facilities, each fixture type shall be in accordance with ICC A117.1 and each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall. Distribution of the sexes is not required where single-user water closets and bathing room fixtures are provided in accordance with Section 2902.1.2.

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole number; one fixture for the number of persons shown or any fraction of it.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 2902.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number. | Table footnote a: The fixtures shown are based on one fixture being the minimum required for the number of persons indicated or any fraction of the number of persons indicated. The number of occupants shall be determined by this code.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In each toilet room they may replace up to 67% of the required toilets in assembly (restaurant) and educational occupancies, and up to 50% in all others (offices). Each urinal used by the public or employees needs partitions (screens) at least 60 inches high, starting no more than 12 inches above the floor.
urinal_substitution.quote: 424.2 Substitution for Water Closets. In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies. | 405.3.5 Urinal Partitions. Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy. The horizontal dimension between walls or partitions at each urinal shall be not less than 30 inches (762 mm). The walls or partitions shall begin at a height not greater than 12 inches (305 mm) from and extend not less than 60 inches (1524 mm) above the finished floor surface.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate men's and women's rooms aren't required at a total occupant load of 15 or fewer (any use), 25 or fewer in a business occupancy, or 100 or fewer in a mercantile occupancy.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: 2902.2 Separate Facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: ... Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer.

compartments.text: Every toilet used by the public or employees needs its own compartment with walls or partitions and a door, except in a one-person toilet room with a lockable door.
compartments.quote: 405.3.4 Water Closet Compartment. Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. Exceptions: Water closet compartments shall not be required in a single-occupant toilet room with a lockable door.

occupant_load.text: Office (business areas): 150 sq ft gross per occupant. Restaurant dining room (assembly, unconcentrated, tables and chairs): 15 sq ft net. Classroom: 20 sq ft net. Pennsylvania's regulation makes no change to Chapter 10's table.
occupant_load.quote: Business areas | 150 gross ... Assembly without fixed seats ... Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) | 15 net ... Educational: Classroom area | 20 net

restroom_equity.text: A separate Pennsylvania rule (Restroom Equity Act of 1990, Act 185, 35 P.S. 5820.1 to 5820.6, and its regulations) requires at least two women's toilets for each men's toilet or urinal in 'facilities where the public congregates': sports and entertainment arenas, stadiums, community and convention halls, specialty event centers, amusement facilities, ski resorts, public middle schools and high schools, and community and municipal parks with seating for 500 or more. It applies to new facilities and to renovations that rebuild more than 50% of the building or add to it. Hotels and public eating or drinking places (restaurants) are exempt. Offices are not on the list. The regulation's wording leaves open whether the 500-seat threshold applies to every listed facility or only to parks; the statute itself could not be opened.
restroom_equity.quote: § 50.82 (a) Application. Section 50.81, this section and § § 50.83—50.86 apply to facilities where the public congregates: sports and entertainment arenas, stadiums, community and convention halls, specialty event centers, amusement facilities, ski resorts, public middle schools and high schools and community and municipal parks with a seating capacity of 500 or more persons. ... (b) Exemptions. ... (1) Hotels. ... (2) Public eating or drinking places defined in the act of May 23, 1945 (P. L. 926, No. 369), known as the Public Eating and Drinking Place Law. (3) Community and municipal parks with seating capacity for less than 500 persons. ... (d) Renovating existing facility. An existing facility where the public congregates will be considered to be renovated if one of the following applies: (1) Its rehabilitation requires more than 50% of the gross floor area or volume of the entire building to be rebuilt, not including cosmetic work such as painting, wall covering, wall paneling, floor covering and suspended ceiling work. (2) An addition is made to an existing facility where the public congregates. | § 50.83. Restroom requirements. More water closets shall be provided for women than for men by a minimum ratio of two water closets for women for each water closet for men or for each single use urinal or 20 inches of trough urinal.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Base table only (2021 IBC Table 2902.1). The school rows do not apply the Restroom Equity rule: in a new or more-than-half-rebuilt public middle or high school covered by that rule, women's toilets must be at least twice the men's toilets plus urinals (for example 200 occupants: men 2, women at least 4).

hdpe_fire.section: International Building Code of 2021, Section 803.9, with Section 803.1.1 and the Chapter 2 definition of interior wall and ceiling finish, as adopted by 34 Pa. Code 403.21(a)(1) (Chapters 2 to 10 adopted; the only Chapter 8 change is to Section 803.3)
hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP). Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish, it shall comply with Section 803.1.1. | 803.1.1 Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish Materials Tested in Accordance With NFPA 286. Interior wall and ceiling finish materials shall be classified in accordance with NFPA 286 and comply with Section 803.1.1.1. | [BF] Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish. The exposed interior surfaces of buildings, including but not limited to: fixed or movable walls and partitions; toilet room privacy partitions; columns; ceilings; and interior wainscoting, paneling or other finish applied structurally or for decoration, acoustical correction, surface insulation, structural fire resistance or similar purposes, but not including trim. | 34 Pa. Code 403.21(a)(1)(iii)(A): Section 803.3 (relating to heavy timber exemption) is modified to add the phrase: ‘‘In buildings equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with section 903.3,’’ before the word ‘‘exposed.’’
hdpe_fire.note: Section and definition text read on UpCodes (Pennsylvania Building Code 2021); the official regulation confirms Chapter 8 is adopted with a change to 803.3 only.

access.state_standard: Chapter 11 and Appendix E of the International Building Code of 2018, with ICC A117.1-2009 (the edition the 2018 code's Chapter 35 references), as part of the Uniform Construction Code. The rest of the building code is the 2021 edition, but a court permanently enjoined the 2021 accessibility updates, so the 2018 accessibility requirements still apply. The 2021 existing-building code's accessibility sections (301.5, 305, 1101.2, Appendix B) are excluded by regulation.
access.standard_quote: L&I: On October 26, 2022, the Commonwealth Court issued an opinion in Pennsylvania Builders Association v. Department of Labor and Industry, which permanently enjoined enforcement of the 2021 accessibility updates to the Uniform Construction Code. As such, effective immediately, you must cease all enforcement of the 2021 accessibility standards. Since the 2018 accessibility standards were in effect before December 25, 2021, and were unchallenged, all structures must still comply with the 2018 accessibility requirements. | L&I: Chapter 11, Appendix E of the International Building Code of 2018 and any other accessibility requirements contained in the 2018 I-codes referenced by the Uniform Construction Code were published in the Pennsylvania Bulletin and became effective on June 15, 2019. | 2018 IBC Chapter 35: ICC A117.1—09 Accessible and Usable Buildings and Facilities

differences.point: Vertical grab bar on the side wall
differences.state: ICC A117.1-2009 604.5.1: besides the 42-inch horizontal bar, an 18-inch vertical grab bar on the side wall. Applies to wheelchair stalls (604.9.6) and to both sides of ambulatory stalls (604.10.4).
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.5.1: a horizontal side wall grab bar only; no vertical bar.
differences.quote: 604.5.1 Fixed Side Wall Grab Bars. Fixed side-wall grab bars shall be 42 inches (1065 mm) minimum in length, located 12 inches (305 mm) maximum from the rear wall and extending 54 inches (1370 mm) minimum from the rear wall. In addition, a vertical grab bar 18 inches (455 mm) minimum in length shall be mounted with the bottom of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum above the floor, and with the center line of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum from the rear wall. | 604.10.4 Grab Bars. ... Side wall grab bars complying with Section 604.5.1 shall be provided on both sides of the compartment.
differences.federal_quote: 604.5.1 Side Wall. The side wall grab bar shall be 42 inches (1065 mm) long minimum, located 12 inches (305 mm) maximum from the rear wall and extending 54 inches (1370 mm) minimum from the rear wall.

differences.point: How many wheelchair and ambulatory stalls
differences.state: 2018 IBC 1109.2.2: at least 5 percent of the compartments in a toilet room must be wheelchair accessible (so a second one from 21 compartments up); where compartments plus urinals total six or more, at least 5 percent ambulatory accessible as well.
differences.federal: At least one wheelchair stall, plus at least one ambulatory stall where there are six or more compartments or six or more toilets and urinals combined.
differences.quote: 1109.2.2 Water Closet Compartment. Where water closet compartments are provided in a toilet room or bathing room, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be wheelchair accessible. Where the combined total water closet compartments and urinals provided in a toilet room or bathing room is six or more, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be ambulatory accessible, provided in addition to the wheelchair-accessible compartment.
differences.federal_quote: 213.3.1 Toilet Compartments. Where toilet compartments are provided, at least one toilet compartment shall comply with 604.8.1. In addition to the compartment required to comply with 604.8.1, at least one compartment shall comply with 604.8.2 where six or more toilet compartments are provided, or where the combination of urinals and water closets totals six or more fixtures.

differences.point: Family or assisted-use toilet room in assembly and mercantile buildings
differences.state: 2018 IBC 1109.2.1: assembly occupancies (restaurants included) and mercantile occupancies that require six or more toilets in total, men's and women's together, must also provide an accessible family or assisted-use toilet room (one toilet, one lavatory, door securable from inside), signed with the International Symbol of Accessibility. Its fixtures count toward the required number.
differences.federal: No requirement to provide a unisex or family toilet room in new construction; 213.2.1 only sets what a unisex room contains where one is used (for example in alterations where full compliance is technically infeasible).
differences.quote: 1109.2.1 Family or Assisted-Use Toilet and Bathing Rooms. In assembly and mercantile occupancies, an accessible family or assisted-use toilet room shall be provided where an aggregate of six or more male and female water closets is required. In buildings of mixed occupancy, only those water closets required for the assembly or mercantile occupancy shall be used to determine the family or assisted-use toilet room requirement. ... Fixtures located within family or assisted-use toilet and bathing rooms shall be included in determining the number of fixtures provided in an occupancy. | 1109.2.1.2 Family or assisted-use toilet rooms shall include only one water closet and only one lavatory.
differences.federal_quote: 213.2.1 Unisex (Single-Use or Family) Toilet and Unisex Bathing Rooms. Unisex toilet rooms shall contain not more than one lavatory, and two water closets without urinals or one water closet and one urinal. ... Doors to unisex toilet rooms and unisex bathing rooms shall have privacy latches. | Advisory 213.2: These requirements allow the use of unisex (or single-user) toilet rooms in alterations when technical infeasibility can be demonstrated.

access.same_as_federal: Read and found the same as the 2010 ADA Standards in ICC A117.1-2009: wheelchair stall size (60 in wide, 56 in deep wall-hung, 59 in floor-mounted), toe clearance (9 in high, 6 in deep; 12 in high for children's stalls), self-closing door with a pull on both sides, ambulatory stall 60 in deep (A117.1 says 36 in wide; ADA says 35 to 37 in). A117.1-2009 Table 604.9.3.1 lets the door opening sit either within 4 inches of the far partition or at least 56 inches from the wall nearest the toilet; that is looser than the ADA, not stricter, so the ADA's 4-inch rule still governs.
access.process: No separate state registration or fee-based plan review for accessibility. The accessibility chapter is enforced with the building permit: by the municipality where it employs or contracts a code administrator certified as an Accessibility Inspector/Plans Examiner, otherwise by the Department of Labor & Industry (which also covers opt-out municipalities and all state-owned buildings). Only the Secretary of Labor & Industry can grant a modification, variance or extension of time from the accessibility requirements, on the advice of the Accessibility Advisory Board.
access.process_quote: 34 Pa. Code 403.102(o): The Department will enforce Chapter 11 (Accessibility) of the Uniform Construction Code and other accessibility requirements contained in or referenced by the Uniform Construction Code until a municipality employs or contracts with a code administrator certified as an accessibility inspector/plans examiner under this part. | 34 Pa. Code 403.142(a): The Secretary has the exclusive power to grant modifications and extensions of time and decide issues of technical infeasibility under Chapter 11 (Accessibility) of the Uniform Construction Code and other accessibility requirements contained in or referenced by the Uniform Construction Code for individual projects

single_user.rule: Under the building code adopted statewide, single-user toilet rooms and family or assisted-use toilet rooms count toward the required fixtures and must be identified as available to all persons regardless of sex. No separate Pennsylvania statute on single-user restroom signs was found. For state-owned buildings, a Department of General Services policy (4 Pa. Code Chapter 67b) calls for at least one universal single occupancy restroom on each floor with restrooms in new capital projects, with the Department's sign.
single_user.quote: [P] 2902.1.2 Single-User Toilet and Bathing Room Fixtures. The plumbing fixtures located in single-user toilet and bathing rooms, including family or assisted-use toilet and bathing rooms that are required by Section 1110.2.1, shall contribute toward the total number of required plumbing fixtures for a building or tenant space. Single-user toilet and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet rooms and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex. | 4 Pa. Code 67b.4(a): At least one universal single occupancy restroom will be created per floor/story for each floor/story that contains restrooms in all Capital Projects for new construction.

all_gender_shared.rule: Allowed. Separate men's and women's rooms aren't required where rooms with toilets and lavatories are designed for use by both sexes and every toilet has its own compartment with walls or partitions and a door. Urinals must be in an area visually separated from the rest of the room or each in a stall (the fixture-calculation section says each urinal in a stall). The fixture count is then based on the total occupant load. The model code text has no exception for schools.
all_gender_shared.quote: 2902.2 exception: Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by both sexes and privacy for water closets are installed in accordance with Section 405.3.4 of the International Plumbing Code. Urinals shall be located in an area visually separated from the remainder of the facility or each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall. | 2902.1.1 exception: Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load. In such multiple-user user facilities, each fixture type shall be in accordance with ICC A117.1 and each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall.

use_restrictions.rule: No Pennsylvania statute restricting who may use which restroom in government buildings, schools or private buildings was found (one web search; the legislature's site was not searched bill by bill). A bill of that kind was reported as introduced and referred to committee, not enacted. Treat as 'none found', to be confirmed.
use_restrictions.note: Search result summaries only: a legal-analysis piece states there is no state law in Pennsylvania that specifically addresses transgender students' access to bathrooms; a 'Two Gender Protection Act' bill was reported as referred to the Senate State Government Committee.

public_wage.law: Pennsylvania Prevailing Wage Act (Act of August 15, 1961, P.L. 987, No. 442; 43 P.S. 165-1 et seq.). Rates and job classifications are determined by the Department of Labor & Industry, Bureau of Labor Law Compliance, for each project, by craft and county.
public_wage.threshold: Project's estimated total cost over $25,000; construction, reconstruction, demolition, alteration or repair other than maintenance work; paid for in whole or in part out of the funds of a public body (school districts included). A project may not be divided to fall below the threshold.
public_wage.quote: Pennsylvania Prevailing Wage requirements govern a public work. A public work requires the unconditional payment of prevailing wage rates if it is: Construction, reconstruction, demolition, alteration and/or repair work other than maintenance work; ... Paid for in whole or in part out of the funds of a public body; and The project’s estimated total cost is over $25,000 (A project may not be divided into components or separate projects to fall below the $25,000 threshold.) | The prevailing wage rates are determined by the Department of Labor & Industry for the actual work performed based upon the workers’ job classification and the locality of the work being performed. The rates are based upon collective bargaining agreements and other data for the craft and classification in the county where work on the public works project is being performed. | Labor and Industry issues prevailing wage rates for each project. ... The Pennsylvania prevailing wage rates should be contained in the bid specifications issued for a public works project. | Maintenance work is the repair of existing facilities when the size, type or extent of the facilities is not changed.

pending_change.text: L&I's prevailing wage page carries a notice that Act 101 of 2026 was signed on October 22, 2026 and takes effect December 21, 2026. A search result (LegiScan, not opened) describes it as Senate Bill 908, amending the Prevailing Wage Act's definitions, specifications and duty of secretary. The act's text was not read.
pending_change.quote: Governor Shapiro signed Act 101 of 2026 on October 22, 2026, and it goes into effect on December 21, 2026. The Department is assessing enforcement and compliance requirements and will provide more information soon.

local_note.text: 1% local tax is added in Allegheny County (Pittsburgh: 7% in total) and 2% in Philadelphia (8% in total). Nowhere else in the state.
local_note.quote: The Pennsylvania sales tax rate is 6 percent. By law, a 1 percent local tax is added to purchases made in Allegheny County, and 2 percent local tax is added to purchases made in Philadelphia.

shipped_goods.rule: Taxable. An out-of-state retailer with more than $100,000 of gross sales into Pennsylvania in the previous calendar year must hold a sales tax license and collect. If the seller doesn't collect, the buyer owes use tax at the same rate (state plus the local 1% or 2% where delivered or used) directly to the Department of Revenue.
shipped_goods.quote: REV-717: Every person, association, fiduciary, partnership, corporation, or other entity making taxable sales of tangible personal property or services must obtain a Sales Tax license. This includes out-of-state retailers who make more than $100,000 of gross sales into Pennsylvania in the previous calendar year. ... Entities which make taxable purchases but did not pay sales tax upon purchase should report and pay use tax directly to the department | Use tax page: When Pennsylvania sales tax is not charged by the seller on a taxable item or service delivered into or used in Pennsylvania, the consumer is required by law to report and remit use tax to the Department of Revenue. The use tax rate is the same as the sales tax rate: 6 percent state tax, plus an additional 1 percent local tax for items purchased in delivered to or used in Allegheny County and 2 percent local tax for Philadelphia.

freight.quote: 61 Pa. Code 54.1: (a) Effective March 4, 1971, separately stated delivery charges billed by the vendor made in conjunction with a taxable transaction are subject to tax. ... (c) Charges for delivery made by someone other than the vendor and billed by someone other than the vendor are not subject to tax. | REV-717: Tax is to be collected on the full purchase price without any deduction on account of the cost of labor, shipping, handling, delivery, or installation.

install_labor.rule: Depends on whether the installed item becomes a permanent part of the real estate. Attaching property to real estate so that it becomes a permanent part is a 'construction activity', and the regulation presumes that 'Partitions (attached by means of bolts or screws)' and 'Lavatories (partition, soap dispenser, toilet tissue dispenser, towel dispenser, dryer, urinal, mirror)' become a permanent part of real estate. Labor is taxed where the vendor installs property that stays personal property ('sales activities'), even if billed separately. No Department text read addresses, in so many words, an installer fitting partitions the owner bought separately; under the definition it is a construction activity, not a taxable sale.
install_labor.quote: 61 Pa. Code 31.11: Construction activities—An activity resulting from an agreement or contract under which a contractor attaches or affixes tangible personal property to real estate so as to become a permanent part thereof. Construction activities also include the service of repairing real estate even though tangible personal property is not transferred by a contractor in conjunction with the repairs which he makes. In the absence of satisfactory evidence to the contrary, the following items are presumed to become a permanent part of real estate: ... Lavatories (partition, soap dispenser, toilet tissue dispenser, towel dispenser, dryer, urinal, mirror) ... Partitions (attached by means of bolts or screws) ... | 61 Pa. Code 31.12(b)(3): Effective March 4, 1971, charges for labor or transportation in conjunction with the sale at retail and installation of tangible personal property are subject to tax even though the labor or delivery charges are separately stated on the billing.

furnish_and_install.rule: A construction contract. The contractor pays sales or use tax on the partitions and other materials it furnishes and installs, and does not charge the customer sales tax on the job; it may build the tax into its price but not show it as a separate item. The contractor generally cannot use the customer's exemption (government, school district, charity) for materials that become part of the real estate; a narrower exemption exists for 'building machinery and equipment' on contracts with exempt entities.
furnish_and_install.quote: 61 Pa. Code 31.12(a)(1): A contractor shall pay tax upon the purchase price, as defined by the TRC, of all property, including materials, equipment, components and supplies, which he furnishes and installs in the performance of his construction activities. Example 1: ... The dishwasher becomes a part of the realty and is included in the overall price of the house to the customer. ‘‘X’’ Contractor does not charge sales tax on this transaction to his customer. The contractor may include the tax he must pay in his bid proposal but not as a separately stated item. | 61 Pa. Code 31.13(a): ... a contractor erecting a building, repairing a roof, replacing a door for a governmental agency, manufacturer, processor, public utility, school district, charitable or religious organization, and the like, shall pay tax upon the property which he consumes and is not entitled to use the exemption of the ultimate customer for whom he is performing the contract. | REV-717: Generally, construction contractors are required to pay tax on all property (including materials, equipment, components and supplies) that is furnished and installed in the performance of construction activities.

(xii) Movable cases, counters and partitions that are not over 5 feet 9 inches in height. | (d) An ordinary repair does not require a permit. The following are not ordinary repairs: (1) Cutting away a wall, partition or portion of a wall.

page.stalls_intro: Pennsylvania's rules count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women, and any fraction rounds up. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in each men's room they may take the place of up to half of the required toilets in an office, and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, and each urinal needs a screen.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and the men's figures show toilets only, before any are swapped for urinals. An office with 25 people or fewer, or any space with 15 or fewer, can use one shared restroom. A separate Pennsylvania law asks for two women's toilets for every men's toilet or urinal in new or largely rebuilt public middle and high schools, arenas, stadiums and convention halls, so ask your building code official whether it covers your project.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Pennsylvania's building rules treat toilet partitions as an interior finish and require solid plastic (HDPE) and polypropylene partitions to pass a room-corner fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use, and a room with six or more toilets and urinals also needs a narrower stall with grab bars on both sides. Federal law and Pennsylvania's building rules set the sizes. Access is checked with the building permit, by your local code office or, where it has no certified access inspector, by the state Department of Labor & Industry. Only the state can approve an exception.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Pennsylvania extras:** Pennsylvania goes further than the federal rules in three places. The accessible stall needs an 18 inch vertical grab bar on the side wall as well as the horizontal one. In a very large restroom, 5% of the stalls must be wheelchair accessible, which means a second one from 21 stalls up. And a restaurant or store that needs six or more toilets in total must add a one-toilet family restroom.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone. A shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and urinals are in stalls or screened from view. We found no Pennsylvania law that limits who may use which restroom.
page.public_jobs: on projects paid for in whole or in part with public money and costing more than $25,000, school district work included, Pennsylvania law requires at least the wage the state Department of Labor & Industry sets for each trade in the county; maintenance work is not covered.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in Pennsylvania, a contractor who supplies and installs partitions that are bolted or screwed to the building doesn't charge sales tax on the job, and pays the tax on the materials instead. State tax rules presume that partitions fixed this way become part of the building. They don't spell out the case of an installer fitting partitions you bought yourself, so ask.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxable, and so is delivery charged by the seller. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the state.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue
